weeks.title: Introduction to software analytics
weeks.subtitle: Research questions, data and defensible evidence
weeks.connection: Project: define a research question, unit of analysis and data source.

lessons.title: Begin with a decision
lessons.text: Software data becomes useful when it supports a concrete engineering decision. Before choosing a technique, name the question, the people who will use the result, and what action could change. “Find technical debt” is incomplete until you define what counts as an admission of debt and how a reviewer would use a finding.

lessons.title: Define one observation
lessons.text: A comment, a class, a commit and a service incident are different units of analysis. Their labels and dependencies differ too. Repeated comments from the same project are not necessarily independent evidence. Record the population, sampling rule, identifier and target before calculating a metric.

lessons.title: Make the comparison fair
lessons.text: A keyword rule offers explicit matching behavior; an LLM can use context but may produce unsupported explanations. Compare them on the same records, preserve uncertainty, and inspect disagreements. A plausible explanation is a hypothesis to verify. The small annotation exercise teaches this process; it does not establish general model superiority.

papers.connection: Frame the comment-labeling task around a review decision.

weeks.title: Reading and reviewing empirical research
weeks.subtitle: Claims, evidence and exception-handling failures
weeks.connection: Assignment 2: operational definitions and paper critique. Project: identify a claim to investigate.

lessons.title: Reconstruct the argument
lessons.text: Read a paper as a chain: research question, data, operational definition, method, result and inference. For each central claim, record the exact section, figure or table that supports it. Distinguish what the authors measured from the broader interpretation you might be tempted to attach to it.

lessons.title: Review the evidence
lessons.text: Ask who or what is missing from the sample, how labels were created, and which alternative explanations remain. A prevalence study describes observed patterns; it does not by itself show that removing those patterns prevents failures. A useful review identifies a consequential limitation and a feasible way to investigate it.

lessons.title: Use a model as a critic
lessons.text: Complete your own review and manual annotation before asking a model to critique them. Check every citation and quotation against the assigned paper. Agreement between annotators can reveal consistency, but agreement alone cannot validate the coding scheme. Preserve “uncertain” when a scenario omits the contract needed to judge it.

papers.idea: Study production failures and the testing opportunities they expose.
papers.question: How does the sampled failure population limit the conclusion?
papers.connection: Use the paper’s actual cases for reading. Lab scenarios are authored teaching examples, not extracted incidents.

papers.idea: Operationalize anti-patterns and measure their prevalence.
papers.question: Does a detectable pattern necessarily imply a harmful behavior?
papers.connection: Use the assigned definitions for Assignment 2. Preserve the distinction between detection and contextual assessment.

weeks.title: Source code and exception handling
weeks.subtitle: From syntactic rules to policy-aware analysis
weeks.connection: Assignment 2: separate detector findings, policy judgments and evaluation targets.

lessons.title: Patterns are operational definitions
lessons.text: A detector translates a paper definition into observable syntax or program behavior. AST rules can recognize a catch body or caught type, but names alone may miss bindings and propagation. Record the exact rule, scope, location and unresolved cases so that another researcher can reproduce your counts.

lessons.title: Context changes the judgment
lessons.text: A structural pattern and a harmful behavior are separate targets. The same shape can implement an intentional policy in one setting and violate a required contract in another. Analyze the handler, caller expectations and propagation path. Do not silently label an unknown contract as safe or harmful.

lessons.title: Connect detection to the papers
lessons.text: The ORM reading demonstrates operationalizing performance anti-patterns. Exception-flow analysis motivates following behavior beyond a local handler. EH-Fixer brings contextual reasoning and repair into the discussion, while this lab remains Java detection and assessment. A detection result is not evidence that a generated repair is correct.

weeks.subtitle: JDT visitors, boundary tests and contextual evidence

lessons.title: Build a testable detector
lessons.text: Write the expected behavior of boundary cases before running the implementation. Include relevant positive, negative and unresolved cases. Comments, nested handlers and qualified names can expose differences between text matching and AST analysis. A parse or binding failure belongs in an explicit status field, not in the negative class.

lessons.title: Control retrieved context
lessons.text: A context agent chooses what information to inspect through a declared read-only interface. Limit the available tools and decision budget, and record every observation. To understand why retrieval helped, give a fixed prompt the same retrieved context. This separates the benefit of information from the benefit of orchestration.

lessons.title: Explain the implementation
lessons.text: A successful demonstration connects a predicted result to the actual AST or binding evidence. Each contributor should explain a failure mode and make a small tested modification. The notebook records the experiment; it does not replace the required JDT implementation or establish binding correctness by itself.

weeks.title: Developer comments and technical debt
weeks.subtitle: Text classification, project transfer, and grounded explanations
weeks.connection: Assignment 3 Q1: group comparisons, sampling, magnitude and uncertainty.

lessons.title: Learn from developer text
lessons.text: Self-admitted technical debt is an admission of a limitation or compromise in developer text. Keyword rules can miss implicit statements and flag ordinary uses of technical words. TF–IDF learns a vocabulary from training data; an LLM interprets wording. Both need a documented labeling contract.

lessons.title: Hold out the project
lessons.text: Shared vocabulary and duplicated comments can make evaluation deceptively easy. Keep projects separated and fit the vocabulary on training projects only. Choose a threshold on validation, then freeze it before testing. Curated class balance changes what accuracy and precision mean for deployment.

lessons.title: Move from comments to review metrics
lessons.text: The Qt extension studies a different unit: components with measured review activity and outcomes. Inspect distributions, compare magnitude and uncertainty, and consider alternative explanations such as size and prior defects. A difference in an observed metric is not automatically an effect of changing review practices.

weeks.title: Software metrics and explanatory modeling
weeks.subtitle: Association, uncertainty, and auditing an analysis agent
weeks.connection: Assignment 3 Q2–Q3: explanatory modeling and verified effect interpretation.

lessons.title: Specify an explanatory question
lessons.text: An explanatory model describes conditional associations under a stated specification. Define the outcome, measurement timing and proposed predictors before fitting. Skew, missing data and correlated size metrics affect both the sample and interpretation. Report what was excluded and why.

lessons.title: Interpret the actual scale
lessons.text: A coefficient for a transformed predictor is not a change per original unit. Odds, probabilities and expected counts are different quantities. Use a meaningful predictor contrast and a stated covariate scenario to verify an interpretation. An uncertainty interval that includes a null value does not establish an exact zero effect.

lessons.title: Audit a model plan
lessons.text: Give the independent agent a schema and permitted training summaries, then ask for a structured plan. Validate columns and transformations before trusted code executes it. Compare choices and assumptions with your reference model. An absent term means it was not included, not that its coefficient was estimated as zero.

papers.title: Studying the Relationship between Logging Characteristics and the Code Quality of Platform Software
papers.idea: Traditional lens: measure logging and examine its association with code quality.
papers.question: Why might logging correlate with defects even if logging is useful?
papers.connection: Confounding example: difficult code may need more logging and also contain more defects.

papers.question: What must be checked beyond whether generated code executes?

weeks.title: Execution logs and event templates
weeks.subtitle: Parsing quality, parameter boundaries, and downstream errors
weeks.connection: Project option: log parsing and its downstream analytical consequences.

lessons.title: Abstract messages into events
lessons.text: An event template separates meaningful constants from changing values such as identifiers. Masking too much merges different events; masking too little splits one event into many. Template choices therefore affect downstream counts and rare-event detection.

lessons.title: Measure two different properties
lessons.text: Grouping agreement asks whether records are partitioned together. Exact recovery asks whether the template preserves the correct constants and variables. A parser can group consistently while producing the wrong text. Evaluate systems separately and inspect both merge and split errors.

lessons.title: Compare parsers on matched records
lessons.text: Implement a transparent conventional parser and ask an LLM to infer templates for the same fixed IDs. Keep reference templates outside the prompt, validate coverage and retain failures. The regex lab transfers ideas from the readings; it is not an implementation of Logram or the full LogParser-LLM system.

papers.question: What does an event abstraction preserve or discard?
papers.connection: Compare recovered log structure with the constants and wildcards in our parser.

papers.question: Which frequency assumptions break for rare events?
papers.connection: Our regex baseline is a simpler teaching comparator, not a Logram reproduction.

papers.idea: LLM lens: infer log structure using language-model capabilities.
papers.question: How should parsing quality be balanced against model calls and context cost?
papers.connection: Compare template inference, reuse, and evaluation. A plausible template still needs exact validation.

weeks.title: Performance telemetry and root cause analysis
weeks.subtitle: Multimodal evidence, bounded investigation, and abstention
weeks.connection: Project option: evidence-based diagnosis across metrics, logs and traces.

lessons.title: Align the incident timeline
lessons.text: Metrics, logs and traces may use different timestamp units and sampling windows. Normalize time before joining evidence and state the display timezone. The preceding interval is a comparison window, not a certified healthy baseline. A window median may dilute a short or late event.

lessons.title: Separate symptoms from causes
lessons.text: A large metric change identifies a candidate, not a cause. Inspect timing, alternative explanations and dependencies. Trace parents can be missing because of roots, external calls or sampling; nested span durations cannot simply be summed into end-to-end latency. A component mapping must be supported by evidence.

lessons.title: Bound an investigation
lessons.text: A diagnostic agent should gather bounded observations through declared tools and return evidence, uncertainty and alternatives. Compare metrics-only and multimodal conditions under a fixed budget. Localizing a component and explaining a mechanism are separate judgments; abstention can be appropriate when the supplied evidence is insufficient.

papers.title: Automatic Identification of Load Testing Problems
papers.idea: Traditional lens: diagnose problems using measurements collected during load testing.
papers.question: What must remain comparable across baseline and incident runs?
papers.connection: Identify workload changes that could mimic a fault.

papers.idea: Traditional lens: combine counters and logs to investigate memory-related problems.
papers.question: Which independent observations would corroborate a memory hypothesis?
papers.connection: Ask whether a counter change is a cause, symptom, or recovery signal.

papers.title: OpenRCA: Can Large Language Models Locate Root Cause of Software Failures?
papers.idea: Agent lens: investigate software failures using operational evidence.
papers.question: How should tool use, diagnosis quality, and investigation cost be evaluated?
papers.connection: The lab uses small adapted windows and a bounded tool controller, not the full benchmark.

lessons.title: Predict with information available then
lessons.text: Incoming-change prediction uses information available at a decision time. Chronological splitting helps, but author timestamps do not prove when defects were discovered. Audit feature timing, labeling delays and project boundaries before making a deployment claim.

lessons.title: Evaluate the review budget
lessons.text: Average precision describes ranking; a fixed threshold produces hard decisions. Inspection effort adds another question: how many labeled risky changes can be found within a limited review budget? Changed lines are a proxy, not human time. Count whole commits and declare how ties are handled.

lessons.title: Control the information advantage
lessons.text: A diff-informed LLM sees information that a numeric metric model does not. Compare numeric-only, diff-only and combined conditions when attributing gains. The sample uses functional defect labels; it cannot directly reproduce PerfJIT’s performance-regression target. Freeze prompts and thresholds before testing.

Require a structured model plan; validate features, transformations and model family before trusted code fits it. Save every decision/observation. Audit one consequential disagreement and allow one documented correction before freezing the plan. Compare reference, independent and corrected plans using training-only validation.
